text.tspan: App.tsx is 11,450 lines with 184 useState hooks; api.ts holds the whole route table and every handler in 3,098 lines. Both are the top fan-out files.
The browser bundle imports 60+ symbols from src/server (parser, text, features, members…). Shared domain code lives under the server's name and ships to the client.
server ↔ plugins/host (15/36), server ↔ automerge (17/22), server ↔ git (3/19), and one 11-file cycle: state, auth, tokenStore, repo, demoMode, git/cli, git/js, git/gh…
confluenceStorage (server) imports frontend/markdownSyntax, testref, weblinks; server/proposals imports the gateway. Lower layers reach up.
SDK is a façade over internals.
@specdriven/host re-exports ~20 server modules plus the Automerge store, so third-party plugins couple to core file layout, not to a stable API.
tests, issues, pages and self-fix are plugins in name; their panes and logic sit in src/frontend, and the plugin client only mounts them.
isDemoMode() is called at 26 sites in 10 files, hostedMode is read in 12; each new mode adds another if-branch across layers.
Confluence, qTest and Aha each get Tokens + Url + Token.tsx + PublishDialog (≈2.1k lines; the three token modules differ by 39 lines). Electron's main.ts imports all four token stores.
Two API entry paths (note, by design).
Electron calls handleApi over app:// without requestGuard, so the guard lives in the web server's fetch rather than in the API itself.
